stories.author: @svenstevenson2245
stories.text:
Honestly really didn't like 10-2 as a game.

The not true new game+, the way they structured the game; I only ever did one play through because I didnt realize the first time through that doing the essential missions locked you out of the early stages of other side quests.


The semi bastardization of one of my favorite FF mechanics, namely job/job change system.

The thinly veiled charlies angles rip off theming.

Lastly, while I did not like how 10 originally ended, it was by no means, a bad ending, just not the one I wanted, there are many times I've felt this way in the past, just because the ending was not the one I wanted does not mean the ending was bad, but 10-2 retconned the ending and with some half hearted bullshit too.

Anyways all this was to say that, this song however, even to date haunts me... brings back such a strong sense of nostalgia and longing for the past and times long gone, for things before they changed and things I will never regain... this and 1000's words were the only parts of this game I found redeemable.

stories.author: @davidjturner
stories.text:
Replayed this game this past month for the first time since it released in the States. Actually blown away by how well it has aged. There's some cringe in there, but if you can get through it, it represents the apex of the ATB system in FF and arguably the best of the job system as well, rolled into one. A campy romp through old stomping grounds culminating in an emotional ending, and it's kicked off by the best track the game has to offer right up front on the menu. Didn't hurt that it was my first time being exposed to everything the International release added.

These fantasy worlds we experienced when we were children really did become a part of us. Something magical about coming home for awhile.

stories.author: @deaththeclover
stories.text:
I fell in love with this theme when I heard it. It gives off *SOO* much story, like that feeling of: peace has finally come at last. 

Everyone is living happily! Wakka and Lulu are legendary guardians watching over the town and their newborn baby, stepping into parenting together. The Besaid Aurochs are still doing what they do best, practicing for the next blitz season ready for whatever challenges await them. Now they are probably known as the best team all throughout Spira.

But under all the happiness of this song, there’s a tinge of something missing, a burning feeling of sadness. For many people, its the sadness of Tidus not being around to enjoy the peace he helped bring to Spira. But for me it’s the feeling of *NEVER* being able to experience the story and the world SE sprung to life for the first time ever again. That alone just breaks my heart...

stories.author: @OpenOceanOnly
stories.text: The original Besaid theme is one of my favorite instrumental tracks of all time. I absolutely hate the "re-master" version, but I forgot how good the FFX-2 version is. It seems to be an "answer" to the original: the FFX version has a feeling of being in awe of the natural beauty around you while also having the repeating, dissident low tone to remind you of the impending doom that is Sin. This version has a feeling of bittersweet memories mixed with the comfort of home, since it is the place Yuna can most call home. People think Nobuo Uematsu is the be-all-end-all of Final Fantasy music, but people forget that two other composers worked with him for FFX (one of whom made the original Besaid track) and he had no involvement with the series after that.

As I get older, I lose more and more family and friends. Naturally.

The meaning just keeps changing as I regret not telling some of my family how much they truly meant to me before they were gone. Regrets mount like nothing I’ve ever felt before. Naturally. 

I guess I’m really thankful for this song. It’s helped me understand in so many transforming ways in my life that it’s… this song is my golden rule. Always just say “I love you.” when you leave.
